Keeps Andy in front of him!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: They only cost a hundred and twenty dollars!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Yeah, that's a lot of money for most people.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: I don't understand why all of you poor people don't just get more money.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: You really don't know how money works, do you?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: You use it to buy stuff! It's not that hard!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Still, I can't accept this.
Owen hands the shoebox back to Paige. She takes it and immediately dumps it in the trash!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: What are you doing?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: I don't need them!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Yeah, but you can't just throw a new pair of sneakers in the trash!
Owen slaps the lid off the trash bin and starts rooting around in the garbage.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Gross. If you ever want to know why I don't respect you, this is why.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Wasn't asking!
Owen comes out of the garbage holding the shoebox...

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Is there a day when you `don't` smell like the underarms of a P.E. teacher?
nodes.text_bbcode: Is there a day when you [color=#3b78e2][i]don't[/i][/color] smell like the underarms of a P.E. teacher?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Is there a day when you don't look like the--
Paige slaps Owen! Then she marches off down the hall!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Ow! You didn't even hear what I had to say!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: I know enough! Have fun with your stupid basketball tryouts! I hope you trip on your shoelaces and break your ungrateful arms!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: That could have gone a lot better...

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: This feels like the kind of gift you'd give, you know...
Paige bursts into laughter!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: If you think I want you as my boyfriend, then you're delusional.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Am I? Something happened between us, and I don't know what to make of it.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Well neither do I!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: So are we going to do anything about it?!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: I don't know! What are we supposed to do?!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I don't know.
Owen and Paige are silent for a moment. Then both of them say, at the same time--

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Maybe we should talk--

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: I guess we could talk--

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Oh. Uh, go ahead.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: No, you.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Can we talk about this later?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Maybe. Why not now?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I really don't want to be distracted during tryouts.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Fine then. We'll talk about it later.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: In the meantime, why don't you suck up your pride for a second and just wear these shoes for the tryouts?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I really don't know how I feel accepting a gift from you.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: What else am I going to do with them?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Take them back?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Do I look like someone who `takes stuff back?`
nodes.text_bbcode: Do I look like someone who [color=#3b78e2][i]takes stuff back?[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Fine. I'll wear them.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Whatever. I'm already over it.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Paige, seriously, this is really nice of you... Are you feeling okay?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Hey! I do nice things!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Like what?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Occasionally, I'll give one of my credit cards to someone homeless!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Don't they just run up a huge tab?!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Ew! Not for `spending!` I give them my expired ones... You know, for fantasizing.
nodes.text_bbcode: Ew! Not for [color=#3b78e2][i]spending![/i][/color] I give them my expired ones... You know, for fantasizing.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I was going to suggest you go to the nurse's office. But never mind. You're definitely yourself.
Paige playfully punches Owen in the arm.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Shut up!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Heh. Now I really have to go. Bye, Paige.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Bye, Owen... And don't suck today.
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Thanks.
Owen walks toward the gym, the shoebox tucked under his arm, a broad smile on his face.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I'm really sorry that it had to be this way. That you and Howard couldn't be together. If it were up to me, you'd be able to be happy all the time.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: That's... That's really sweet, Owen...

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Well, you're really--

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Ahem. Am I interrupting something?
Paige approaches them, carrying a shopping bag.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: ...No, Paige. Actually, um, I... I... Should be going. Bye, Owen.
$ZOE hastily walks away down the hall.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: I'm `so` glad I didn't win Social Chair. Getting bossed around by Taylor. It's like $ZOE has to work all the time!
nodes.text_bbcode: I'm [color=#3b78e2][i]so[/i][/color] glad I didn't win Social Chair. Getting bossed around by Taylor. It's like $ZOE has to work all the time!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I can see how that might seem hard for someone who doesn't work at all.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: As if. You always make me sound so lazy. Do I have to remind you that I was the one who made the Halloween carnival happen?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: You or your servants?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Grr...

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Relax, relax, I'm just teasing.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Actually, I should probably get going too, I've got basketball tryouts in a few minutes.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Duh. Spencer's been talking about it in class non-stop. It was obnoxious, to say the least.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: He kept going on and on about how awesome it was going to be...

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: And about how your shoes were, like, super pathetic.
Paige reaches into her shopping bag and pulls out a shoebox. She hands it to Owen.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: What's this?

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Just open it, would you?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Uh... Okay.
Owen opens up the shoebox to reveal a new pair of high-end basketball shoes!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Whoa! These are expensive!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Are they? I just got whatever was on the shelf... Er, of the garage. The garage shelf.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: They used to belong to one of my servants or my servant's servant or something removed from me.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: But these are brand new. And they're in my size.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: I don't know what to tell you! My servant's servant or whoever must have had the same size feet as you... And obviously got bored of a boring game!

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Are you satisfied, Detective Owen?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Uh huh. Seriously, Paige. These are... These are great, but I don't know if I can accept them.

nodes.speaker: Paige
nodes.text: Why not?

options.label: I don't know what we are.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: I know what you meant, Owen.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Oh, sorry.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: No, it's okay! It's good to get it out there.
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: So... You're doing good?

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: I'm doing... As good as a girl whose first love is gone.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: So... Not good at all then?

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Pretty much.
$ZOE holds up her poster gear.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: It's nice to have this Social Chair work as a distraction.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: What stuff are you talking about?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Stuff. Stuff with... You know. Howard.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: You don't have to tiptoe around it. I'm a big girl.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Sorry...

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: It must be hard. You two seemed so close. The way everyone talks, it's like you were soulmates or something!
$ZOE tries to hide her tears, but Owen still notices.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I'm sorry!

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: No, I'm sorry! `Sniffle!`
nodes.text_bbcode: No, I'm sorry! [color=#3b78e2][i]Sniffle![/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: No, I shouldn't have said that! I'm really sorry!

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: It's okay. I'm okay. I'm okay.
$ZOE turns from Owen for a moment, dabbing at her eyes with a piece of poster paper. She turns back to Owen.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Well, we're both very sorry, aren't we?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: It seems that way. So I guess I shouldn't talk about...

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: It's fine. Hearing that thing about soulmates got me. I'm better now.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: You're sure?

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: This time I'm sure. I'm a big girl. For real.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I just wanted to say...
The silence between them is overwhelming. Ben knows the night is ruined.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: So, I guess I'll just be going home then?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Yeah, that'd probably be best.
He heads for the door, worry knotting its way through his stomach.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I hope I didn't just completely blow things with Emily...
You are now playing as Owen.
After school, Owen's on his way to basketball tryouts when he runs into $ZOE. She's holding poster paper and some markers.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: $ZOE... Uh, hi.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Hey, Owen. I heard you're trying out for the basketball team. Nervous?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: A little. But it can't be more nerve-racking than when we raced back here to get to the State Championship game in time!

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Hee... I remember that. Ben was so paranoid he was going to get a speeding ticket! He took all the backroads to avoid the cops!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Heh. I'm pretty sure we drove through a park!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: So what's the poster gear for?

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Taylor wants me to make posters for the upcoming Snow Ball. Life of the Social Chair.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: And... Um... How are you doing?

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Good... I'm good.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I meant, you know, now that...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I don't think that's true at all!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: You don't?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: No! What happens if the person you're with is doing something horrible or dishonest or wrong?!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: If anything, in those cases, it's the other person's responsibility `not` to support them!
nodes.text_bbcode: If anything, in those cases, it's the other person's responsibility [color=#3b78e2][i]not[/i][/color] to support them!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I never thought about it like that...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Well, you haven't been thinking much lately, have you?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Oh...
Emily gets quiet, not saying anything.
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I guess quiet is better than angry.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Just out of curiosity, your basketball experience level is...?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Zero. None. Bottom experience level.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Ben! Why didn't you say you were joining something you're actually interested in?!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Like what? Slacker Group? Party Team? Makeovers Anonymous?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I'm serious!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I kind of am too. I mean, your dad is not totally off-base about me.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Really? You're agreeing with my father? The guy who just made me and the entire swim team risk our lives climbing a mountain in a storm?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Your relay times `have` improved.
nodes.text_bbcode: Your relay times [color=#e23b3b][i]have[/i][/color] improved.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Ugh! Not the point!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I know. And I get your point. But I'm saying I need to grow up more.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: You're already grown up enough, Ben. You don't need to change anymore than you already have!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Maybe I haven't changed enough! Maybe joining the basketball team will be the next best thing for me!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Well, let me know how it goes.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: You're not going to watch my tryout?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: No! I'd rather you face the music and come clean.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: You mean, tell your father that I lied to his face?! I made a mistake, but confessing it now isn't going to make things better.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: So?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: So I'm going to tryout for the team tomorrow, and I could really use your support.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Why does my support matter?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Because...

options.label: Couples support each other no matter what!
I feel better when you're around!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Can you imagine how that dinner would have gone if I hadn't made that up?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Yes...
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I'd still be Ben, the gargoyle-stealing crime lord.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: It wasn't going very well.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: So you see why?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Yeah, I do, but that doesn't mean I think it was right.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I want my dad to like you... Your lie might have saved tonight, but at the cost of the future.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: What happens when he finds out you're not actually a basketball wizard?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I didn't think of that...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Do you think my dad has any say over who I date?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I don't know... He can be pretty forceful.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I'm not asking for his approval, you know that, right?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I guess I do now.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Also, guess what? A guy my dad loves is probably `not` going to be the guy I love.
nodes.text_bbcode: Also, guess what? A guy my dad loves is probably [color=#3b78e2][i]not[/i][/color] going to be the guy I love.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Maybe I'll go back up there and tell him I'm quitting school and joining a metal band.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Very funny, but you're still in a lot of hot water with me.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Lying to him is not cool, Ben! Especially if you're doing it because you think it will help us.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I know...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: The basketball team? Really? That's news to me!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: And to me!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: And to me!

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Why did you decide to join? It seems... Out of character.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Well, I, uh... I really admire the discipline that comes with organized sports.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: You're just filled with surprises!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Tell me about it...

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Oh, and, uh, Emily's work ethic is so inspiring, I thought it might push me the same way swimming pushes her.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: And here I was thinking you were just some casual, tennis-playing slacker.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Basketball's been a hobby of mine for a while. It's an addicting sport. Love to, uh, love to `hoop.`
nodes.text_bbcode: Basketball's been a hobby of mine for a while. It's an addicting sport. Love to, uh, love to [color=#e23b3b][i]hoop.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: I've never heard it phrased that way before.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Yup. That's what we call it. Me and all the other... `Hoopsters.`
nodes.text_bbcode: Yup. That's what we call it. Me and all the other... [color=#e23b3b][i]Hoopsters.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: What's your skill level?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Skill level? Probably top... Top skill level.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: You must play as a guard, right? Small guy like you.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: That's right! I'm your typical guard, `obviously,` because of my size.
nodes.text_bbcode: That's right! I'm your typical guard, [color=#e23b3b][i]obviously,[/i][/color] because of my size.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Hmm. Well, once again, I seem to have misjudged you, son.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: I'll be looking forward to watching your games.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: That's `if` I make the team. Tryouts are tomorrow. Competition could be fierce!
nodes.text_bbcode: That's [color=#e23b3b][i]if[/i][/color] I make the team. Tryouts are tomorrow. Competition could be fierce!

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Ha! If you're a top-level guard, there's no way you'll get cut from our sorry excuse for a basketball team!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Well, um, then I guess I'll just have to make the team.
The rest of the dinner proceeds smoothly, with Coach Kessler easing up on Ben and sharing stories about his days as a swimmer...
Afterward, Ben and Emily are sitting together on the couch in the den.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I think your dad started to warm up to me... Again.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Uh, yeah, because you completely lied to him!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I'm really sorry about lying, Emily. But what was I supposed to do? If I told the truth...

options.label: He'd have even less respect for me.
We'd never be able to date.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Your decision to eat steak?! How does that prove your commitment to discipline?!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: It takes a disciplined mind to eat red meat even when you know it's unhealthy!

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: That's downright idiotic.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Are you okay? What are you talking about?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I'm sorry... That's not what I meant to say at all.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I meant to say that I'm... Uh...
Ben reflects on his time in the gym earlier that day...

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I'm thinking about joining the basketball team!

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: To eat the basketball team?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: What?! No!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Ben! What are you saying?
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Join! I meant join the basketball team!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Uh...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Say something!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Steak!

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: To join...?
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Uh... To join...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: To eat...?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Uh...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Spit it out!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: To eat!
Coach Kessler picks up the carving knife and gestures at Ben with it.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: I'm going to speak my mind now, because that's what I do in my house.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: I do not understand you. You don't really seem to have any focus or discipline. To me, you're just a boy whose only concern is getting his next dose of fun!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Dad!

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: My daughter seems to like you, but that doesn't mean I do. In fact, it pretty much guarantees I don't.
Coach Kessler cuts off a hunk of his steak.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: That's all there is to say.
A heavy silence fills the room.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Kessler
nodes.text: Well, who's up for ice cream?
Mrs. Kessler gets up from the dining table and beelines for the kitchen. Emily stares at Ben, her eyes pleading for him to say something.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: You know, sir, there's something I've been meaning to tell you that, uh... That addresses exactly what you just said.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Something that, uh, that `proves` my commitment to discipline!
nodes.text_bbcode: Something that, uh, that [color=#e23b3b][i]proves[/i][/color] my commitment to discipline!

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: And what's that?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Uh... I am, of course, talking about... My decision...

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: It had been sitting in an abandoned house for years, collecting cobwebs and dust! Whoever owned it decided they didn't want it a long time ago!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: It wasn't serving any purpose except as a scary story that was relevant once a year.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Getting it for $ZOE not only made her haunted house better, it also might have been the deciding factor for her winning Social Chair!

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Hmmph.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: What my dad means by that is 'Wow. That actually sounds like a really nice thing you did, Ben.'

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: I'll do my own speaking, young lady.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Sometimes you need a translator.

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Kessler
nodes.text: I'd buy one of those.
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Ha!

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Don't encourage them.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: It wasn't just me. It was Spencer and--

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Are you going to tell me that criminal behavior is okay if you have company?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Uh... Now that you put it that way, no.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: If your friends jumped off a bridge into shark-infested waters, would you jump too?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Not sure the waters need to be shark-infested for this example...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: What did you say?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Nothing!

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: And that's a pretty good start! Not much else except--
Spencer notices Owen's ratty, torn shoes.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Dude! `Dude!` You `have` to get new shoes!
nodes.text_bbcode: Dude! [color=#e23b3b][i]Dude![/i][/color] You [color=#e23b3b][i]have[/i][/color] to get new shoes!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: What's wrong with these?

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: What's wrong? They look like puppets! Your shoes are so torn up, they're talking to me when you walk!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: They're not `that` bad... But maybe I should buy some new ones...
nodes.text_bbcode: They're not [color=#e23b3b][i]that[/i][/color] bad... But maybe I should buy some new ones...

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Please. Just... You have to. Nothing is more important than shoes, bro.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Anyway, haven't you forgotten other major parts of the game, like shooting?

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Pfft. You think the top football guys like us actually need `help` putting a ball through a dumb ol' hoop?
nodes.text_bbcode: Pfft. You think the top football guys like us actually need [color=#e23b3b][i]help[/i][/color] putting a ball through a dumb ol' hoop?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Yes! I do! It seems like a `completely` different skill set!
nodes.text_bbcode: Yes! I do! It seems like a [color=#e23b3b][i]completely[/i][/color] different skill set!

nodes.text: The bell rings, signifying the end of the lunch hour.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Oh. Well, we're out of time.
Ben hops down from the bleachers.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Fun times. Love spending my lunch not eating in a sweaty room.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Are you okay?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: No... Actually, I think I'm just anxious about this dinner I'm having tonight with Emily and her dad.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Coach K! That guy is a scary dude!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Try dating his daughter... And then having dinner with him... In his house.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: The worst kind of home court advantage!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Hold up... I thought you guys were cool after the last Kessler dinner?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: He found out about the party that was going on at my house that same night.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Weak.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: And about the gargoyle I stole from the haunted house for the Halloween Dance.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Super weak.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Back to square one?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Yeah, I always feel like I'm not nearly man enough to even be in his presence.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: So then man up, Kale!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Normally, listening to Spencer is a bad idea. But this might be one of those times where he's right.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Yeah! When you see him, instead of shaking his hand, just give him a manly chest bump!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Er... Spencer's right about the 'man up' part... But don't do that.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Got a better idea?

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Yeah. Just be yourself. And when the moment to step up comes, just get your mouth moving. The right words will come.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: We'll see...
At the Kessler house that night, Coach Kessler sits at the head of the table, a large carving knife beside him, the blade facing Ben.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Last time it was a sword, now it's a carving knife! What is up with the sharp objects in this house?!

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: So... How's your career as an irresponsible party thrower going?

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Kessler
nodes.text: Dear, must we go through this again?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Yeah, Dad, you already grilled him once. And he passed, remember?

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: That was before I heard about the gargoyle!

nodes.speaker: Mrs. Kessler
nodes.text: I saw the photos from your dance, Emily! That statue was very scary-looking!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Ben got it for $ZOE's haunted house! Wasn't that `nice` of him?
nodes.text_bbcode: Ben got it for $ZOE's haunted house! Wasn't that [color=#3b78e2][i]nice[/i][/color] of him?

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Correction. Ben `stole` it for $ZOE's haunted house.
nodes.text_bbcode: Correction. Ben [color=#e23b3b][i]stole[/i][/color] it for $ZOE's haunted house.

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Being responsible and spending quality time with you is `nice.`
nodes.text_bbcode: Being responsible and spending quality time with you is [color=#e23b3b][i]nice.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Committing a felony is another matter! We clearly have different definitions.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Ahem. Sir, if I could clarify...

nodes.speaker: Coach Kessler
nodes.text: Go ahead. Clarify. I'm `very` interested to see how you get out of this!
nodes.text_bbcode: Go ahead. Clarify. I'm [color=#e23b3b][i]very[/i][/color] interested to see how you get out of this!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I'm not trying to get out of anything, sir. I got the gargoyle...

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Not like I'm going to need to know anything about basketball...
Ben types out a text to Emily...

nodes.speaker: Phone
nodes.text: in gym. spencer giving owen bball tips. yawn x 1000.
Ben types out the text.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: ...And send. Time to play my favorite mobile game!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Can I catch the killer? Yes, I can! Bring it!
His phone beeps. It's a reply from Emily.

nodes.speaker: Phone
nodes.text: lol youre so funny!
His phone beeps again.

nodes.speaker: Phone
nodes.text: excited for dinner tonight with my dad at least.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Oh yeah, real excited for that. What boyfriend wouldn't be excited to spend time with their girlfriend's crazy, alpha male, overprotective father?
Ben types out a text: 'me too! should be fun.'
As Ben sends it, he hears Spencer wrapping things up with Owen.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Who knows? Maybe someday I'll need to know this stuff.
Ben watches and listens from the bleachers...

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: One: You can't just carry the ball like you do in football. You have to dribble.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I've seen that in video games.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: If you stop with the ball and move one of your feet, your other foot is called your `pivot foot.` If you lift it, that's traveling.
nodes.text_bbcode: If you stop with the ball and move one of your feet, your other foot is called your [color=#e23b3b][i]pivot foot.[/i][/color] If you lift it, that's traveling.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: NEVER LIFT YOUR PIVOT FOOT!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I'm right here.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Two: No tackling.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I knew that one.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: I didn't. A couple of guys at the courts near my house were pretty surprised.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Instead of tackling, you've got to stay in front of your opponent. You do that by `sliding your feet` and `keeping your butt down!`
nodes.text_bbcode: Instead of tackling, you've got to stay in front of your opponent. You do that by [color=#e23b3b][i]sliding your feet[/i][/color] and [color=#e23b3b][i]keeping your butt down![/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Same as when I dance!

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Got it?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Got it... Defense is just like getting your moves on at a slamming party!

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Kale! I wasn't asking you!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Oh, right.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Yeah, I got it.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Three: Every time someone shoots, put your back to your opponent and push them away from the hoop! It's a rebounding technique called `boxing out.`
nodes.text_bbcode: Three: Every time someone shoots, put your back to your opponent and push them away from the hoop! It's a rebounding technique called [color=#e23b3b][i]boxing out.[/i][/color]

nodes.text: He finds a nearby seat in the bleachers.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Wait... You said my head's not clear. How is my head not clear?

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: For real? These last couple weeks you've been... What has he been, Kale?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Distracted.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Distracted!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: How have I been distracted?

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: In History class today, you told the teacher that Benjamin Franklin should have run for Social Chair!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: To Owen's credit, Ben Franklin would have thrown some sick parties!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: So I said that. That's just one slip up.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: The other day you handed me a tater tot and told me to 'eat my oats.'

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Ha! You called me `Prissy.`
nodes.text_bbcode: Ha! You called me [color=#e23b3b][i]Prissy.[/i][/color]

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I think it's because of my hair...
Owen sighs.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Paige owns a horse, and she's friends with Prissy. I guess I've got her on my brain. I don't know what's going on with us.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Dumb. Play basketball. Then you'll be thinking about points, cheerleaders, and... Not Paige.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Spencer does have a certain undeniable logic sometimes.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Fine. It couldn't hurt to tryout. So, why are we here and not, you know, actually eating lunch?

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: We're here because basketball `isn't` football.
nodes.text_bbcode: We're here because basketball [color=#e23b3b][i]isn't[/i][/color] football.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: The hits just keep on coming.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: We don't know basketball like we do football. If we're going to crush tryouts, we can't just coast on our athleticism. We also need to know the game.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: First, we'll go over the basics...
Ben's phone beeps.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: It's a text from Emily...

nodes.speaker: Phone
nodes.text: bored. what u doing?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Uh...

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Do I have to spell it out for you?
Ben doesn't respond, as though his brain isn't working.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Hey, that's cool. Sports are to me how analogies are to you, Spence.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: What?
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Never mind. I'll just be spectating from the bleachers.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Uh, okay. You asked for it.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: You're a nerd, Ben. That means you study and do nerd stuff like play with dolls.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Action figures!

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Whatever. Owen and I, we're athletes. We play sports.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: So, you're discouraging me from trying out because you don't think I've got much of a chance?

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: No... I'm discouraging you because I think you have `no chance.`
nodes.text_bbcode: No... I'm discouraging you because I think you have [color=#e23b3b][i]no chance.[/i][/color]

nodes.text: Ben's stomach drops.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Fine. I'll be over here.
Ben dribbles down the court. At first, it's difficult for him to do so without looking at the ball, but he manages to reach the far baseline.

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: Now pivot and come back!
Ben pivots perfectly and dribbles back toward the team. This time he's able to dribble the entire length of the court without looking at the ball once!
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: That wasn't too hard!

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: Nice job, son.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: How'd you do that, Kale?!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I dunno. I just kinda did it.
Ben has failed.

nodes.text: The rest of the players take their shots. Once everyone's had their chance, all the players line up on the baseline.
Coach stands in front of them, a scowl twitching at the edge of his mouth...

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: I've made my decision! It was not a hard one!
He points at a handful of players and separates them to one side. Ben is among them.

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: All of you are cut!
Coach gestures to the other group, the one Ben's not in.

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: The rest of you made the team!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I... I didn't make the team.
As the rest of the players celebrate, including Spencer and Owen, Ben trudges off the court toward Emily.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: So... What now?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I think there's only one thing to do...

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Yes. Finally you're going to come clean and tell my dad you lied to him about being an athlete?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: That wasn't what I had in mind.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: What then? What are you going to do?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I've just gotta find the right sport!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: That's a horrible idea! You're not an athlete, Ben!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Oh yeah? Just watch me!
In the aquatic center...
Ben flails his arms about, splashing water every which way as he tries to complete a freestyle lap.
Cameron stops him, treading water nearby.

nodes.speaker: Cameron
nodes.text: I know a lot about swimmers. How can I put this delicately? You are... Not one of us.
Ben manages to grab onto the pool edge, grateful for the relief.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I know there's a sport for me somewhere.

nodes.speaker: Cameron
nodes.text: Well, it's probably on land.
In the hallway...

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: So, what do you think, Nate? Can I play football? I can catch!
Ben hands Nate a football and runs a route down the hall.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I'm open!
But Nate has already thrown the ball! The moment Ben turns, the ball cracks him in the nose!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Owwwww! My nobe!

nodes.speaker: Nate
nodes.text: I thought you said you could catch!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I thod I coub!

nodes.speaker: Nate
nodes.text: Now might not be the best time to tell you that football season is over.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Yed. Now id nod da best tibe...
In the gym...

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: So that's why I'm pretty sure cheerleading is my calling! I've got lots of enthusiasm!

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: No way. It gets weird with guys on the team.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I'm pretty sure that's discrimination...

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Besides, Hector and Keith are already on the team.

nodes.speaker: Nicole
nodes.text: Yeah, but Hector is like forever with Amanda! So obnoxious!

nodes.speaker: Jill
nodes.text: And Keith's still hung up on his ex-girlfriend. Neither of them will try to make a move on us.

nodes.speaker: Hector
nodes.text: We're right here.

nodes.speaker: Keith
nodes.text: It's so weird that you girls talk about us like we don't exist.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Wait... So, if me hitting on you is the issue, it's not an issue at all. I've got Emily!
All the cheerleaders stare at each other in stunned silence.

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: Then... You haven't heard?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Heard what?
$ZOE puts a comforting arm around Ben.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: Ben, Emily broke up with you.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: No, she didn't! If she broke up with me, I would've known.

nodes.speaker: Zoe
nodes.text: You've been so wrapped up in trying to find a sport for you, you just completely abandoned Emily.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: She would've told me!

nodes.speaker: Maria
nodes.text: She did tell you, you idiot! You just didn't hear her!

nodes.speaker: Nicole
nodes.text: She also changed her Faceplace status to: Ben, if you ever actually have enough time to read this, we're over.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Then, that's it... I lost her.

nodes.speaker: Amanda
nodes.text: It's okay, Ben! I'm still with Hector! Yay!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Thanks, Amanda.

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: I'm not going to make the team. This game's too hard. I can't make a layup!

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: I didn't get a rebound! Rebounds are my bread and butter! My waffles and syrup!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I don't know if I made it either...

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Are you kidding? You're like the best player, Kale! I don't know how, but you are.
Coach points at a handful of players and separates them to one side.

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: All of you are cut!
He points to the group Ben is now standing in.

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: You six, you're my team!
Ben looks around him... At Spencer, Owen, Andy, Jacob, and Erik.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I made the team!
The other players sulk off the court and out of the gym.

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: Congratulations! To celebrate we're going to follow tradition and meet at the pizza place near my apartment.

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: It's called Mario's. It's in the hills. See you all there.

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: Awesome! I love Mario's!

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Best pizza in town, hands down!

nodes.speaker: Erik
nodes.text: Yes! Mario's pizza makes my stomach gurgly!
As the Coach walks away, Emily runs over to Ben!

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Ben! That was incredible! When did you become a basketball player?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Heh. Just now, I think.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: My dad's going to be so impressed.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Yeah, I can hear him now, 'What'd you have to do to make the team? Show up? Grumble grumble grumble. No one is right for my daughter!'

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Ben!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Sorry, that got away from me.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Want to hang out and celebrate at my house?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Uh... I do, but the Coach wants us to meet for pizza. Wanna come with us instead?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I don't know if I have time, since I have to be up early for swimming tomorrow... Where is it?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: It's at this place called Mario's in the hills.

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: No, I definitely don't have time for that...

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: It's not that big of a deal if we don't hang out. I mean, we can always hang out tomorrow, right?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Yeah. Sure.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: You're okay?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: I think so.
The guys are about to leave the gym.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Yo, Kale! You coming?

nodes.speaker: Andy
nodes.text: Pizza waits for no man!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: So, then, I'll see you tomorrow?

nodes.speaker: Emily
nodes.text: Right.
Emily walks away from Ben. He walks toward the guys and glances back to Emily.
And he knows from the look on her face that something is definitely wrong.

nodes.text: Without a moment's hesitation, Ben shoots, the ball arcing high in the air... And through the hoop!
`Swish!`
nodes.text_bbcode: [b]Swish![/b]

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: Nice shot, boy!

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: What!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Ben is actually... A really good shooter!
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I made it!
Ben freezes!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: A lot of pressure!
Right when Ben's about to shoot, Coach blows his whistle, startling him!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: `Yah!`
Ben's shot misses the entire hoop!

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: You're taking too long, son! Gotta be quick! No one gets that kind of time to shoot!
After the rebounding drill, Coach stands near the three-point line with a ball.

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: This is the last drill! You're going to get the ball behind the three-point line, turn, and shoot.

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: You each get `one` shot! Why only one? Because I want shooters who can shoot under pressure!
nodes.text_bbcode: You each get [color=#e23b3b][i]one[/i][/color] shot! Why only one? Because I want shooters who can shoot under pressure!

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: If you can't summon the will to make this shot, how are you going to do it in the game with your mommies and daddies and girlfriends in the crowd?!
Ben looks to the empty bleachers...

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I wish Emily were here...

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: Kale, you're up first!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Yes, sir!
Ben heads out to the three-point line...

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I don't know the first thing about shooting.
He picks up the ball...

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Maybe I should just close my eyes.
He feels the weight of the ball in his hands as he turns...

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Or maybe I should just give up.
Then he sees Emily tiptoeing quietly into the gym, watching him expectantly. She smiles at him.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: She's here!
Ben turns his back to Andy, pushes him backwards, and completely locks him out from the hoop!
The ball bounces off the rim and right toward Ben! He leaps forward and grabs it out of the air!
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Yes!

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: Good rebound!
Ben tries to keep Andy in front of him but he has no idea where the ball is!
He sees Andy's eye go wide, and he turns...
Just in time for the ball to smack him in the face!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: `Ah!`
nodes.text_bbcode: [color=#e23b3b][i]Ah![/i][/color]

nodes.text: Andy scoops up the ball!

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: Ha! We don't rebound with our face, kid!
Ben freezes up!
Andy runs past him, and Ben completely loses track of where the ball is!
He turns...
Ben whispers to Spencer.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Uh, boxing out?

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Kale! I explained this in the gym yesterday!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Could you explain it again?

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: No! There's no time! Figure it out!
Ben watches as Jacob dribbles by himself all the way down to the other end.

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: Unbelievable! My mother could do a better job and she's got a bum hip!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I'd like to see that...

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: All right, everyone! Time for rebounding!

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: I got this!

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: Half of you on offense, half of you on defense!

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: When I shoot the ball, the defense needs to box out and get the rebound!
Ben bends over at the waist...
Ben keeps his butt down low and slides his feet quickly from side-to-side, staying in front of Jacob!

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: That's what I'm talking about! Now come back!
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Good so far!
Ben manages to stay in front of Jacob the whole way back!

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: Grr!

nodes.speaker: Owen
nodes.text: Nice D, Ben!

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: What the crap, Kale! When did you become an All-Star?

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Overnight?
Ben completely freezes, standing there like a moron!
Jacob can't get around Ben!

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: Stop cheating!
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Don't take your frustrations out on me!
Ben goes in the wrong direction!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Uh oh!
Ben hesitates, just standing there like a total moron.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: What am I doing?!
Ben goes in the complete opposite direction!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Whoops!
Ben slides to his right, staying in front of Jacob!
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Hot feet! Hot feet!

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: Grr!
Ben just stands there like an idiot as Jacob blows past him!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: What was I thinking?!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Slide my feet. Keep my butt down. Just like I'm dancing.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Bet you're happy you paid attention!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Big time!
Coach hands the ball to Jacob.

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: Jacob is the best dribbler we had on the team last year. He's going to dribble up the court, and each of you are going to play defense against him!

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: Do `not` try to steal the ball from him! All you have to do is stay in front of him!
nodes.text_bbcode: Do [color=#e23b3b][i]not[/i][/color] try to steal the ball from him! All you have to do is stay in front of him!

nodes.speaker: Jacob
nodes.text: If you can...

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: All right. Ready? Go!
Ben awaits his turn. Spencer whispers to Owen and Ben in the line.

nodes.speaker: Spencer
nodes.text: Just remember what I talked about when we were in here yesterday.
Erik easily catches the ball and they make it down and back the rest of the way without problems!
Score Up!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: Pretty good job, Erik! I thought you said you weren't that good at passing...

nodes.speaker: Erik
nodes.text: Well, I've often found that modesty is the only plant worth cultivating.

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: That was surprisingly profound.

nodes.speaker: Erik
nodes.text: I got it from a fortune cookie. Although, personally, I'm more of a begonia fan!

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: Stop yapping, Nancies! You haven't made the team yet! Time for the defense drill!
The ball smacks Erik square in his...

nodes.speaker: Erik
nodes.text: Tenders! My tenders!
Erik doubles over and falls to the gym floor!

nodes.speaker: Ben
nodes.text: I'm `so` sorry, Erik!
nodes.text_bbcode: I'm [color=#e23b3b][i]so[/i][/color] sorry, Erik!

nodes.text: Coach blows his whistle!

nodes.speaker: Coach
nodes.text: Unacceptable! Did you not hear me?! Chest to chest!
Erik slowly rises to his feet.

After the tryouts, Emily's walking home from school, when $ZOE pulls up alongside her.

Uh huh...

No... It's not bad.

Pretty much. I'm really happy for him.
Really? Because to be honest, you don't `seem` happy.

Were you supposed to hang out tonight?

But one night can easily become two nights and two can become three and before you know it I'm sending him pics of what I look like so he doesn't forget my face!
I think you might be exaggerating the situation... Just a little bit.
Maybe...
Okay, I am. But we just got over all this drama about my friendship with Cameron. I don't want any more.
You'll be fine. I'm sure of it! Ben's the same way Howard was... He's not going to let anything get in the way of your relationship!
You think?
I know it.
$ZOE gives Emily a big smile as she pulls up to Emily's house.
Thanks...
Wow... I just dumped all my problems on you, and I have to get to bed soon. I'm so sorry.
Don't worry about it.
How are you though?
Good. Pretty good.
At least, that's what I keep saying...
It must be tough now without Howard.
Very... But I've kinda sorta done this part already, you know? Plus, there's--
$ZOE stops her sentence short.
There's what?
Nothing.
`Nothing,` eh? What's `nothing's` name? Is it Nate?
$ZOE smiles, but she keeps quiet.
I see. Not ready to share yet?
Not yet.
If you ever want to share... You know you can talk to me, right?
Yeah...
Emily leans across and hugs $ZOE.
